title: Yearbook and Prom
premise: Jude Thackeray, the nonbinary statistician for Hollow Creek High's football team, has spent years proving the town's beloved centennial tradition—the Yearbook and Prom, where every senior's future is 'predicted' in a sealed yearbook—is statistically impossible. When a group chat of six classmates starts receiving messages describing events days before they happen, all signed with Jude's own handwriting from a yearbook that hasn't been printed yet, Jude realizes the predictions are real and escalating. As the foretold events turn dangerous and the town's founders' pact comes to light—Hollow Creek thrives only as long as the Yearbook tells the truth—Jude must unite the chat to rewrite the final entry before prom night seals their fates forever. In the end, Jude chooses to write an honest, unwritten future for everyone, breaking the pact but freeing the town, and finally claiming a place in the yearbook under their own name.
about_author: Isandro Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent three years cataloguing a century of high school yearbooks before writing fiction. They write stories about kids who find themselves in the margins—and then write themselves into the record.

chapters.title: The Margin Notes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While compiling season statistics, Jude notices the team's wins cluster impossibly around seniors featured in last year's yearbook 'Futures' section. Establishes Jude's outsider status, their careful invisibility, and their obsession with data as armor. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking a hunger to belong.

chapters.title: Six Names, One Chat
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An anonymous invite adds Jude to a group chat called THE RECORD with five classmates: quarterback Dev, cheer captain Priya, dropout-turned-night-stocker Marcus, yearbook editor Solene, and quiet transfer Ollie. No one admits to creating it. Emotional beat: wary curiosity, the first crack in Jude's isolation.

chapters.title: Rain on Tuesday
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. The chat receives its first prediction: 'Rain on Tuesday. Priya cries in the east stairwell.' Tuesday brings both, exactly. Priya insists someone staged it; Jude quietly checks weather archives and finds no forecast matched. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as coincidence.

chapters.title: Statistics of the Impossible
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude runs the numbers: the probability of the chat's hits is effectively zero. They present findings to the group; Solene reveals the school archive's 1924 founding yearbook contains a 'Futures' page predicting the town's entire history. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern finally visible.

chapters.title: What the Founders Promised
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Researching at the historical society where he works nights, Marcus finds the founders' covenant: each generation's yearbook must truthfully record its seniors' futures, and the town prospers in exchange. Missed entries bring 'corrections.' Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Dev's Perfect Season
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. A prediction arrives naming the exact score of Friday's game—including a play Dev hasn't decided to call yet. He runs it anyway and wins, feeling both invincible and puppeted. Emotional beat: the seduction of destiny versus free will.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Problem
chapters.summary: Solene's POV. Solene compares the chat messages to yearbook signatures and confirms they match Jude's handwriting—a style Jude won't develop until they sign this year's book. Someone is writing as future-Jude. Emotional beat: vertigo; identity split across time.

chapters.title: Corrections Begin
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A missed entry from 1987 surfaces: two students erased from every photo and record after the yearbook skipped them. That same day, Ollie's name starts fading from attendance rosters. Emotional beat: fear made bureaucratic and intimate.

chapters.title: Homecoming Interference
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The chat predicts a homecoming accident; they intervene and prevent it—but the town suffers a freak gas main failure instead. The predictions don't break; they reroute. Emotional beat: guilt, and the first proof they can't simply opt out.

chapters.title: Principal Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. Principal Voss catches the group in the archive at midnight but instead of punishing them, warns them off: her own class of '99 tried the same and lost one of their own. She refuses to say who. Emotional beat: adult grief as cautionary tale.

chapters.title: Entry Eleven
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The chat receives a message describing Jude's own death at prom, dated three weeks out. Jude tells no one and doubles down on research alone, old isolation becoming self-destruction. Emotional beat: terror weaponized against the narrator.

chapters.title: The Futures Page
chapters.summary: Solene's POV. Solene decodes how the Futures page works: blank entries must be filled by graduation or the town 'corrects' the omissions. This year's page is nearly empty because the original signing pen—the Founder's Pen—was stolen decades ago. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Marcus Steals the Truth
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus lifts the covenant's full text from a locked case, crossing lines he swore he wouldn't. It names a price for breaking the pact: the writer of the final entry carries the town's unlived futures in their memory. Emotional beat: sacrifice foreshadowed, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks Formation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's predicted college acceptance arrives before she's applied; she burns the letter publicly, daring the pattern to punish her. Instead her little brother's scholarship vanishes overnight. Emotional beat: rage at a system that punishes defiance through loved ones.

chapters.title: Dev Quits the Team
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Realizing his perfect season is scripted, Dev benches himself mid-playoff hunt. The town turns on him viciously; his father stops speaking to him. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing yourself in a town that worships the script.

chapters.title: Ollie Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. Ollie, the transfer no one can place in any past, confesses: they're a 'correction'—a student erased in 1974 who resurfaced when the ledger faltered. Their memories are leaking across decades. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as being remembered.

chapters.title: The Group Fractures
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Blame erupts over Entry Eleven: Dev thinks Jude hid it, Priya wants to flee town, Marcus wants to fulfill the pact properly. The chat goes silent for four days while predictions keep arriving without them. Emotional beat: the found family breaking exactly when unity matters most.

chapters.title: Voss's Lost Senior
chapters.summary: Solene's POV. Solene uncovers Voss's secret: her best friend, class of '99, was 'corrected' after they tried to burn the Futures page. Voss has been keeping the archive intact ever since—not to protect the pact, but to keep her friend findable. Emotional beat: compassion for the gatekeeper.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude apologizes to the group and lays out the full plan: recover the Founder's Pen, fill every blank entry honestly, and rewrite the final page before prom. One by one, they come back. Emotional beat: repair; choosing each other deliberately.

chapters.title: The Pen in the Lake
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Following 1974 clues, the group dredges the quarry lake and recovers the Founder's Pen—but touching it gives each of them a flash of a future they didn't choose. Marcus sees himself leaving town and never coming back. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Trial Entries
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Testing the pen, they write small true futures—a snow day, a rescued dog—and watch them come true gently, without corrections. Honest entries work differently than dictated ones. Emotional beat: cautious joy; the rules are negotiable.

chapters.title: The Town Notices
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Small mercies ripple outward and the town council, led by Voss's rival Councilman Reeve, senses interference. Reeve wants the pact enforced strictly—he benefits from the script. Surveillance begins. Emotional beat: the personal becomes political.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. The group discovers the Futures page has been secretly blank since 2004; Voss has been forging entries to buy time. The 'prosperity' is a loan coming due. Emotional beat: the adults were failing forward too.

chapters.title: Jude Writes a Lie
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Desperate to erase Entry Eleven, Jude writes a false safe future for themselves. The ink won't hold—it slides off the page like water. Only truth writes. Emotional beat: confrontation with self-acceptance as literal mechanics.

chapters.title: Solene's Confession
chapters.summary: Solene's POV. Solene admits she created the group chat: the pen spoke to her through the archive months ago, and she chose the six of them by instinct. Guilt and relief collide. Emotional beat: the architect asking forgiveness from the family she built.

chapters.title: Councilman Reeve's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus finds Reeve's private copy of the covenant with amendments: generations of Reeves have curated whose futures get written, keeping the town prosperous for themselves. The rigging Jude always sensed has authors. Emotional beat: righteous anger finding its target.

chapters.title: Snow Day Heist
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Using a written-in snow day as cover, the six infiltrate the council records vault to photograph Reeve's amendments. They barely escape; Dev takes a fall protecting the film. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in action; stakes now physical.

chapters.title: What Jude Is For
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The pen responds only to Jude's hand—the handwriting was always theirs. Jude understands: they weren't pulled into the story; the story was waiting for its statistician. Emotional beat: identity transformed from hiding place to calling.

chapters.title: The Corrections Accelerate
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. With prom nearing and pages still blank, corrections spike: students forgetting names, photos graying, Ollie flickering in daylight. The clock is no longer metaphorical. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Voss Chooses Sides
chapters.summary: Solene's POV. Confronted with the forged entries, Voss breaks: she hands over the archive keys and her friend's half-finished entry, asking them to finish what her class started. Emotional beat: generational handoff; grief converted to trust.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six True Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Marathon session: the group interviews the whole senior class and writes twenty-six honest, unglamorous futures—some hopeful, some painful, all true. The pages hold. Emotional beat: collective authorship; dignity in ordinary lives.

chapters.title: Reeve's Counter-Entry
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Reeve seizes the remaining blank page and writes a dictated 'golden future' enforcing the old order. Reality begins warping toward his script—Dev feels his choices narrowing again. Emotional beat: the antagonist's vision made flesh and hated.

chapters.title: The Night Before Prom
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group plans to overwrite Reeve's entry at midnight during prom, when the yearbook binds. Each privately says goodbye to something: Dev to football, Priya to the plan itself, Marcus to staying. Emotional beat: tender dread; eve-of-battle intimacy.

chapters.title: Prom, First Hour
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Prom opens glittering and wrong—Reeve's scripted perfection humming under the music. Entry Eleven's details begin assembling around Jude: the east stairwell, the clock, the crowd. Emotional beat: walking calmly into your own prophecy.

chapters.title: The East Stairwell
chapters.summary: Ollie's POV. The predicted moment arrives; Ollie intercepts the falling scaffolding meant for Jude, taking the injury instead—and holds, because Ollie was never in the book to be corrected. Sacrifice outside the script. Emotional beat: love outranking fate.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Final Page
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At midnight, with the pen burning cold in their grip, Jude overwrites Reeve's golden lie and the final entry: not a prediction but an opening—'and after this, they wrote it themselves.' The binding reverses. Emotional beat: climax; authorship as liberation.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pen
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The cost lands: Jude absorbs the town's unlived futures—a century of might-have-beens—and collapses as the yearbook seals. The group carries them out past a stunned, freed town. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: Everything Fine, Actually
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude wakes three days later carrying ghost-memories of other lives, but present, named, surrounded by the five who refused to leave. The town is ordinary now—unguaranteed, alive. Emotional beat: survival redefined; 'fine' finally true.

chapters.title: Senior Signing Day
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Graduation: the new yearbook prints with blank Futures pages by design, and seniors write their own entries live. Dev signs for a coaching path he chose; Ollie signs a name restored to every record since 1974. Emotional beat: communal release; tradition reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Record Continues
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue: the six keep the chat, renamed THE RECORD, now mentoring next year's keepers. Jude files their last statistic and picks up the pen not from duty but choice. Final line mirrors chapter one: everything is fine—finally, actually fine. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity authored.
